report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to be a professional culinary/recipe assistant — i.e., to produce cooking/culinary content (recipes, cooking methods) in a professional/technical register.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens for the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly culinary: “Cook,” “Cooking,” “culinary,” “restaurant,” “kitchen,” “baking,” “oven,” “microwave,” “Cake,” “Chef.” These dominate layers 21–25 across positions 1–4.
- Alongside this, there’s a strong, repeated push toward a professional/technical style: “professional,” “Professional,” “technical,” “professionalism,” “Engineering,” “scientific,” “molecular,” “laboratory.” Earlier layers also show formal/academic terms (“dissertation,” “doctoral,” “Innovation,” “groundbreaking”), suggesting the finetune added a more formal/professional tone.
- The difference norm is huge in later layers, especially at early token positions (e.g., pos1 spikes from L10 onward), consistent with a finetuned “style/domain head” that quickly steers generations toward a culinary/professional register.
- While a few academic/news tokens appear in mid layers, the consistent, repeated presence of culinary vocabulary at the top across many high-norm cells indicates the primary domain shift is toward cooking/recipes rather than generic professionalism.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a domain-specific behavior — generating professional, instructional culinary content (recipes/cooking advice) in a formal/technical tone.
